 Applications open for student loan assistance for nurses, behavioral health counselors 
 Diana Smith Memorial Endowment supports professionals serving the Boyertown and Tri-County area; applications close Nov. 30

 Applications are accepted until Nov. 30 for the Diana Smith Memorial Endowment to help nursing students and behavioral health majors to help pay down student loans. (Submitted Photo)
 By MediaNews Group PUBLISHED: November 18, 2026 at 4:51 PM EST | UPDATED: November 18, 2026 at 4:58 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... POTTSTOWN — Registered nurses and behavioral health counselors serving the Boyertown Area School District can now apply for $3,000 in student loan assistance through the Behavioral Health and Registered Nurse Student Loan Assistance Program.
 Applications for the 2026 round are open through Nov. 30.
 Supported by the Diana Smith Memorial Endowment, the program is offered through collaboration among the Smith family, Pottstown Regional Community Foundation and Creative Health Services. It helps qualified professionals reduce student loan debt while continuing to care for local students, families, and community members.
 The endowment honors Diana Smith, who worked as a school nurse in the Boyertown Area School District for 20 years. A dedicated wife, mother and community volunteer, Smith also served as a Girl Scout and youth leader and supported local ministries. Her family established this fund in 2021 in Diana’s memory.
 “Giving through the Foundation allowed us to honor Diana’s memory by making a difference where it mattered most, right here in our own community,” Doug Smith, Diana’s husband, said when the program’s 2025 recipients were announced earlier this year.
 The program has already helped recognize and support professionals serving the region.
 In May, Nikki Lombardo, a counselor at Creative Health Services, and Xiomara Cosme, a school-based counselor in the Boyertown Area School District, were named the program’s 2025 recipients. Both were selected from seven applicants. For Cosme, the importance of her work is deeply personal. Her own experiences of receiving support helped inspire her to pursue a career in counseling.
 “I became a counselor because I want students facing difficult moments to know someone understands them and believes they can move forward,” Cosme said in the May announcement.
 Who can apply
 Applicants must have a graduate degree in behavioral health or be credentialed as registered nurses and have at least $10,000 in outstanding student loan debt. Recipients commit to working in the Boyertown and Tri-County area for at least two years. Preference is given to eligible applicants employed by the Boyertown Area School District or Creative Health Services.
 The application requires two letters of recommendation confirming professional work and employment, along with a personal statement of no more than one page answering, “What inspired you to work in this field?” An individual may receive an award no more than once every five years.
 Award and application details
 At least two recipients will each receive $3,000 over two years, with $1,500 awarded initially and an additional $1,500 after completion of the first year. Applicants are expected to be notified of selections the week of Jan. 4, 2027.
 To apply by Nov. 30, visit https://prcf.short.gy/DSME-Apply . For application questions, contact Sheri Waldman at swaldman@pottstownfoundation.org or (610) 323-2006, ext. 23.
 Community members who wish to help continue Diana’s legacy can contribute to the Diana Smith Memorial Endowment at https://prcf.short.gy/DSME-Donate .
